==Trivia==
* The short story [[Transcript:A Curious Client|A Curious Client]] from the [[Kourend Chronicles]] acts as a prequel to this quest.
** This story implies [[Konar quo Maten]] paid to have the Ancient casket hidden on the mainland, and that [[Veos]] believes it contains a dangerous amulet.
** Upon unearthing the [[Ancient casket]], the player will hear "a faint whispering". In response, they say {{mes|Hmmmm... Must have been the wind.}} This is the same reaction the character in '''''A Curious Client''''' has to the casket talking to them at first.
*** Both the story and the quest are referencing the same phrase popularised by NPCs in the 2006 game {{Wp|The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion}}; Where it signals that an NPC is dismissing suspicious activity, resuming normal behaviour and pretending nothing is wrong. This also echoes similar lines in the {{Wp|Metal Gear}}  (1987 and 1999) and {{Wp|Thief (series)|Thief}} (1998) series.
*Upon release on 7 February 2019, this quest generated some controversy because a house in Lumbridge (which had been unchanged since 2007) was redesigned as a pub and a dock was added to Draynor Village. Some players felt that changes to free-to-play areas (not referenced in the X Marks the Spot poll) were inappropriate without prior consultation from the playerbase.{{CiteNews|author=Jagex|url=https://secure.runescape.com/m=news/boss-heads-and-chambers-of-xeric?oldschool=1|title=Boss Heads and Chambers of Xeric|newsdate=14 February 2019|name=newspost}}
** Due to the controversy from the playerbase, Veos was once again returned to Port Sarim and the Draynor Dock removed in the following update. However, Veos' location was changed from the original southernmost dock to the northernmost dock next to the Port Sarim pub in order to make him more accessible to players.{{NamedRef|newspost}}
* Players who completed X Marks the Spot before Beginner clues were added to the game can claim their own by speaking to Veos in Port Sarim again. Note that you won't receive it by speaking to him at Port Piscarilius.
*This is the only quest that is required for a previously-released quest: in {{UD|Arceuus Spellbook Beta and A Kingdom Divided Preparation|an update}} on [[28 April]] [[2021]], X Marks the Spot was made a requirement for the previously-released quest [[Client of Kourend]].

==Walkthrough==
===The King's Little Dumpling===
{{Needed|recommended=10-14 free inventory spaces to make room for crystalline disks.}}
[[File:King Bolren chathead.png|left]]
Make your way to the [[Tree Gnome Village (location)|Tree Gnome Village]]; the quickest way to reach it is by [[spirit tree]]. Once there, talk to [[King Bolren]] and you'll notice that he has acquired another [[cute creature]], who he's affectionally named "Dumpling". Recognising it as one of [[Glouphrie]]'s [[evil creature]]s in disguise, you will attempt to warn him about its true nature; as usual, however, Bolren will refuse to believe you without sufficient evidence.

Bolren will mention [[Yewnock]], the son of [[Oaknock the Engineer]], who used to visit the village and brought some unusual objects with him. The objects will remind you of Oaknock's machine, and Bolren will recommend you look underground for a local gnome who might know something about an anti-illusion machine.
[[File:Path of Glouphrie puzzle path w-disks.png|alt=Path of push box puzzle|thumb|width=300x300|The path for the monoliths puzzle.]]
Head down to the [[Tree Gnome Village Dungeon]] by squeezing through the loose railing to the south-west and then running east to the dungeon ladder. In the western area of the cave, speak to [[Golrie]] and ask him about a device; if you have not freed him, you will need a [[Key (Tree Gnome Village Dungeon)|key]] to unlock the room he is in, which can be found in the eastern storeroom (inside the crate that looks different than the others).  

Golrie will tell you that his grandfather, [[Bolrie]], used to travel the world collecting elven artefacts and bringing them back to the village, often stashing them in the storeroom nearby. He will tell you that the storeroom is found in the eastern area of the cave, past the tunnel entrance, and that the storeroom's gated strongroom will require a key to enter.

Head to the storeroom by entering the tunnel in the easternmost part of the dungeon, and you will find multiple [[monolith]]s in your way. Push the first monolith north, then search the nearby [[Chest (The Path of Glouphrie, wood)|chest]] for some familiar discs. Next, you will see another four monoliths; push the south-west one north, then the north-west one east. Search the wood chest for more discs, and the silver [[Chest (The Path of Glouphrie, silver)|chest]] for a [[Chest key (The Path of Glouphrie)|chest key]] and [[Yewnock's notes]]. ''You do not need to read the notes, but they will give further lore.''

Push the small monolith south and the north-west monolith west to access the gold [[Chest (The Path of Glouphrie, gold)|chest]], which contains the [[strongroom key]] Golrie mentioned earlier, as well as a [[crystal chime seed]]. Next, inspect the nearby [[singing bowl]] to create the [[crystal chime]], which is needed later in the quest.

===Yewnock's Legacy===
[[File:Argenthorg chathead.png|left|frameless]]
Push the south-east monolith west, then use the [[strongroom key]] on the gate to the west to enter a room with a lectern and [[Yewnock's machine]]. The lectern contains a diary belonging to [[King Bolrie]], who formerly ruled the village; all three chapters will trigger cutscenes, which must be watched to move to the next step in the quest. 

The cutscenes will show an [[advisor]] to King Bolrie, who is tired of the aging [[King Healthorg]]'s inaction against the army of [[General Khazard]]. The advisor suggests to Bolrie that he should campaign to replace the king of the Tree Gnome Stronghold; his opponent [[Argenthorg]], the crown prince, will be "revealed" to care more about humans than gnomes, giving the election to Bolrie. However, sensing foul play, Argenthorg will call upon [[Yewnock]] (son of [[Oaknock the Engineer]]) to activate an anti-illusion machine and expose the advisor as [[Glouphrie the Untrusted]]. Having been tricked, Bolrie is forced to stand down as a candidate to the throne and leave the Tree Gnome Stronghold, as well as abdicate the throne of the Tree Gnome Village.<gallery captionalign="center" widths="200">
The Path of Glouphrie - Bolrie's Diary chapter 1.png|King Bolrie, frustrated at King Healthorg's inaction.
The Path of Glouphrie - Bolrie's Diary chapter 2.png|Campaign posters for the election to become king of the Tree Gnome Stronghold.
The Path of Glouphrie - Bolrie's Diary chapter 3 saboteur.png|A saboteur creates illusions of human food.
The Path of Glouphrie - Bolrie's Diary chapter 3 accused.png|Argenthorg, suspicious of the ruse, gets Yewnock to activate his anti-illusion machine.
The Path of Glouphrie - Bolrie's Diary chapter 3 exposed.png|King Bolrie's advisor is exposed as Glouphrie.
</gallery>{{Colour-shape value|align=right}}
====The Machine====
[[Yewnock's machine]] is similar to [[Oaknock's Machine]] in that players must solve a disc-based puzzle. This time, instead of being given a number you are given the value of the disc(s) to match. In the machine interface, the value of the discs '''inserted on the left''' need to '''add up to the same total value of the one(s) on the right'''. Use the table to calculate the total value of the disc(s) to match, and then solve as before. You will need to match two different values; first, a single shape that adds up to the value of the two displayed at the top, and second, two shapes that add up to the value of the single shape shown on the bottom. 
 
[[Yewnock's exchanger]], located directly next to Yewnock's machine, can be used by first inserting higher valued discs in exchange for multiple lower valued ones, or by combining two smaller discs into a bigger disc. The total value of the input and output will be the same. To operate the machine, click the desired disc in the inventory and then click the disc slot on the machine interface. Then click the double arrows between the two sides to view what will be exchanged. Note that the exchange has three tiers; exchanging a disc in the second slot will exchange for two shapes, and so on.

''Any items left on the ground will disappear following the cutscene.''
{{Listen
|title = [[Dumpling no More (The Path of Glouphrie)|Dumpling no More]]
|align = right
|filename = Dumpling no More (The Path of Glouphrie).ogg
|desc = The jingle that plays upon Dumplings reveal.}}
Once the machine puzzle is successfully solved, a brief cutscene will play where Dumpling is revealed to be an evil creature. Head back up to the village and kill the evil creature, then talk to King Bolren. He will tell you of a gnome explorer named [[Longramble]], who went in search of the lost city, [[Arposandra]]. Though no one knows of his current whereabouts, King Bolren suggests asking [[Gianne jnr.|Aluft Gianne jnr.]] at the Grand Tree for help.

Use the [[spirit tree]] and travel to the [[Grand Tree]]. Bank all unnecessary items (you may safely drop the shapes) and stock up on food and armour. If you're going to trade a [[tangled toad's legs]] for the [[mint cake]] (optional, but highly recommended as the tangled toad's legs is worth {{Coins|{{GEP|tangled toad's legs}}}} and a mint cake is worth {{Coins|{{GEP|mint cake}}}}), be sure to bring it along.<gallery captionalign="center" widths="400" perrow="2">
File:The Path of Glouphrie - Yewnock's machine interface.png|Operating Yewnock's machine
File:The Path of Glouphrie - Yewnock's machine exchanger.png|Operating Yewnock's exchanger
</gallery>

===Arbor Incomitata===
{{Needed|A [[crossbow]] and [[mith grapple]], [[crystal chime]], combat equipment.|recommended=[[Tangled toad's legs]] to receive a [[mint cake]]}}
[[File:Longramble chathead.png|left|frameless]]
[[File:The Path of Glouphrie - grappling to Longramble.png|thumb|300px|The player grapples toward Longramble's coordinates.]]
[[File:The Path of Glouphrie - Incomitatus is healed.png|thumb|300px|Incomitatus is healed to perfect health.]]
Make your way to the Grand Tree, and climb up the ladder once. In the north-west corner, speak to  [[Gianne jnr.]] to learn about Longramble's whereabouts. He will tell you that gnomes have been trying to deliver a dish of [[tangled toads' legs]] to him, but have not been able to reach him. He tells you the coordinates of the delivery is at 2 degrees 7 minutes south and 3 degrees 7 minutes west.

These coordinates will point toward the [[Galarpos Mountains]], just east of the [[Poison Waste]]. The quickest way to travel there is by using the [[fairy ring]] code {{Fairycode|bkp}} and then running north-west; An alternative way to get there is by teleporting to [[Castle Wars]] via [[ring of dueling]], then heading south-west alongside the river. Equip a [[crossbow]] and [[mith grapple]], and cross to the mountain side via the tree in the middle of the river.

Speak to [[Longramble]], who believes Arposandra is close to the Poison Waste. If you brought a tangled toad's legs, he will automatically take it. After going through the dialogue, head further north, and you will feel a strange voice calling to you; this is the [[Spirit Tree (Incomitatus)|spirit tree]] nearby calling you, who tells you to call it [[Spirit Tree (Incomitatus)|Incomitatus]]. The tree's connection to the [[Anima Mundi]], the life force of the world, has been lost due to the toxic waste nearby corrupting its roots, and thus it has fallen ill.

You will mention that how Incomitatus speaks to you through the mind is reminiscent of [[Hazelmere]]'s, and will unintentionally contact him through Incomitatus as the conduit. He will sense that it is unwell, and conclude that the poison seeping into the soil is a byproduct of powerful magic having separated the Anima Mundi from its source. Hazelmere will suggest that healing the tree requires a spiritual cleansing by way of elven magic; he will then notice that you have a set of chimes that can purify it, and ask that you use it on the tree. This will heal Incomitatus, and connects it with the rest of the spirit trees. From this point forward, players can use the tree as a teleport option.

===The Warped Depths===
{{Needed|recommended=[[Earmuffs]] or [[Slayer Helmet]]}}[[File:Terrorbird Guard 21 chathead.png|left|frameless]]
Head west of the spirit tree, and then run south and enter the sewer entrance. You '''do not need''' to fight the [[Warped Tortoise]] at the entrance. ''Note that if you have not yet healed the spirit tree, warped tree roots will block your path after the second warped tortoise.'' [[File:Poison Waste dungeon map.png|thumb|A map of the Poison Waste Dungeon.]]

Once inside, you will need to run a considerable distance to the end of the dungeon; refer to the table below. It is recommended to wear a set of [[earmuffs]] '''''and''''' activate the [[Protect from Missiles]] prayer while traversing the dungeon, as this will negate almost all damage taken. Without ear protection, the [[Warped Terrorbird]]s inside will be able to '''hit through prayers''' with their ranged attacks.

There is a caged hallway at the half-way point where players are safe if they close the gate behind them. Players can also do so in the hallway just before entering the final area.

The level 121 [[Warped Tortoise]]s in the dungeon are not [[aggressive]], but the level 96 [[Warped Terrorbird]]s are, and they use frequent, highly accurate ranged attacks as well as a fairly accurate melee attack. [[Earmuffs]] or a [[slayer helmet]] will reduce the maximum hit of the ranged attacks, '''but the attacks will remain accurate''', so [[Protect from Missiles]] is recommended. Run past them, and avoid stepping on the tar on the ground, as it will turn off [[run energy]] and force you to walk, signaled by the game message {{Mes|You accidentally step in some sticky tar!|colour=red}}.

Head to the end of the dungeon, in a room with a pit in the centre that is connected to three other rooms. To reach the room from the entrance:
{| class="wikitable lighttable"
!Dungeon directions
|-
| Enter the sewer entrance.
|-
| Climb up the ladder.
|-
|Run all the way east. 
|-
|Climb down the ladder.
|-
|Run north and climb up the ladder.
|-
|Run all the way west. 
|-
|Enter the north room. Close the gates and rest here if needed.
|-
|Climb down the ladder in the northern side of the room.
|-
| Run slightly east and climb up the ladder.
|-
|Run north to the room with the pit.
|-
|Enter the east room and fight the terrorbirds.
|}
[[File:The Path of Glouphrie - warped terrorbird fight.png|thumb|300px|Using a pillar to minimise the amount of terrorbirds attacking.]]

The east room contains three [[Warped Terrorbird]]s that must be slain. The terrorbirds use both melee and ranged, and will path towards the player. You must be carrying the [[Crystal chime]] that you sang earlier to harm the birds.

Lower-levelled players can use the pillars around the room to stop the other terrorbirds from attacking. Standing at the door until the three terrorbirds approach you will allow you to engage only one at a time. They may also be poisoned, envenomed, and flinched by trapping them behind the pillars.  They are weakest to crush attacks, and their ranged defence is the strongest defensive stat, but their melee and magic defence is fairly low, and they can be quickly eliminated with any attack style. 

You can also position yourself so that they're not in melee distance (note that they ''can'' melee at a diagonal, unlike most units) so that you only need to pray Ranged. If you are low on prayer and have made sure that all the birds are not in melee distance, you can conserve prayer by only turning it on every 15 ticks once you have successfully prayed against their ranged attack. This is every 5th attack with a shortbow on rapid or every 3rd attack with autocast. ''If you get hit'', they will immediately attack on the 3rd tick after the hit, so be prepared to reset your cycle!

After killing the Warped Terrorbirds, head towards the heavy door on the eastern side of the room to begin a cutscene showing two intelligent terrorbirds, [[Terrorbird Guard 21]] and [[Terrorbird Guard 72|72]], talking to each other. They will lament the boringness of the job, until they notice you and panic, pressing an alarm button that releases tar from the grills. You will try to run but become stuck in the tar, and toxic gases will begin to seep into the room, causing you to become hazy.

As you are about to blackout, [[Hazelmere]] will appear in the nick of time. He activates a special seed pod, the last gift given to him by [[Argento]], which surrounds the both of you with a large aura and teleports you both out to safety. Arriving at his house on the [[Yanille Chain]], he will impart upon you his vision of the future, a vision that heavily involves you and signifies much to come.

<gallery captionalign="center" widths="200">
The Path of Glouphrie - Terrorbird Guard panic.png|The Terrorbird Guards notice your presence.
The Path of Glouphrie - player trapped.png|You are tarred and gassed close to death.
The Path of Glouphrie - Hazelmere appears.png|Hazelmere arrives to rescue the player, activating a special seed pod.
</gallery>

'''Note :''' ''If there is not enough space in the inventory during completion, you can talk to [[Hazelmere]] again to receive the missing rewards. Destroyed lamps can be reclaimed from Hazelmere at any time.''

'''Congratulations, quest complete!'''

==Historical==
[[File:Gielinor Gazette - February 2022 (9).png|thumb|Screenshot from the original Path of Glouphrie quest that was featured in the [[Update:Gielinor Gazette - February 2022|February 2022 Gielinor Gazette]], which discussed porting the quest into ''Old School''.]]
The Path of Glouphrie was originally released in ''RuneScape'' on [[3 September]] [[2007]], 24 days after the [[August 2007 Archive of RuneScape]] that ''Old School'' was built off of. Like other content from the immediate post-backup era (such as the [[God Wars Dungeon]] and [[Land of the Goblins]]), it was present in the archive's files but had not yet been added to the live game.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/718562692177469440|date=8 April 2016|archiveurl=https://reldo.runescape.wiki/i/104933|archivedate=25 May 2020|quote=Yes: Path of Glouphrie and Land of the Goblins. Also Halloween 2007, but we already used that.}}

Jagex first discussed potentially backporting the quest in the [[Update:Gielinor Gazette - February 2022|February 2022 edition of the Gielinor Gazette]]. During the [[April 2023 Game Jam]], it was revealed that [[Mod Ed]] was working on finishing the quest,{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ed|url=https://twitter.com/JagexEd/status/1651202744512831489|date=26 April 2023|archiveurl=https://reldo.runescape.wiki/i/107044|archivedate=27 April 2023|quote=Hey @JagexLenny, things are pretty PoG over here! #OSRSGameJam}} and it was later announced during the [[Summer Summit 2023|2023 Summer Summit]] that the quest would be released sometime in September if it passed [[Poll:Summer Summit 2023 - Giga Poll|the poll]].

===Differences from original version ===
Although identical in premise and concept to the original quest, there are many differences in the ''Old School'' version: 

There are differences in the story and dialogue compared to the original version of the quest.
* Bolren's initial dialogue originally included significantly more information about Yewnock.
* Golrie originally joked about his 'pet' hobgoblins when speaking to him if Roving Elves had been started.
* Speaking to Golrie again after learning about the storeroom from him would originally cause him to talk about how useful items are always found in chests, and how once he explored a temple where the keys to locked doors were always in chests in the rooms he needed them, as a reference to {{wp|The Legend of Zelda}} series.
[[File:King Healthorg turns to stone.gif|thumb|200px|The representation of King Healthorg's death.]]
* Bolrie's diary is almost completely different from the original version:
** In chapter 1, Bolrie was not originally depicted as a king, and did not wear a crown. His advisor originally spoke about how [[General Khazard]] now leads the humans, how they would spell disaster for the gnomes, and how Healthorg and Argenthorg would do nothing to stop them. The advisor advised Bolrie to pre-emptively attack Khazard to win the hearts of all gnomes, and that he would surely be crowned king of the Tree Gnome Stronghold if he did, at which point Bolrie imagined himself wearing a crown.
** In chapter 2, Healthorg's death was symbolically depicted as him turning into a stone statue. Models for this still exist in the game cache.
** In chapter 3, the conversation between Bolrie and Argenthorg was longer, with the additional dialogue depicting Argenthorg as more spoiled and childish. After being exposed, Glouphrie originally had a conversation with Bolrie where he spoke about his motivation to protect gnomes from humanity, and his intentions to found Arposandra. As the cutscene ended, Bolrie originally spoke about pleading with Yewnock to build an anti-illusion machine under the Tree Gnome Village to protect his family, explaining why it's there, which is otherwise unexplained. The cutscene also ended with Bolrie staring at a king statue for a beat before leaving the grand tree.
* As it was originally mentioned in Bolrie's diary, the player character mentioned Arposandra to King Bolren, rather than vice-versa.
* When talking about how to heal Incomitatus, Hazelmere originally explained that elven magic would be required to heal him because [[Seren]] is the divine aspect of the Anima Mundi that the elves revere.
* When mind melding with Incomitatus, there was text explaining how his sickness feels. After being healed, Incomitatus had significantly more dialogue thanking the player and explaining what to do next.
* The final cutscene in the sewers originally had more monologue from the player, as well as more graphical effects, and originally started upon peeking through the door rather than upon defeating all the Terrorbirds.
** The original began with a zoom in through the doors window, and the Terrorbirds frantically jumped around and squawked before pressing the button.
** After the gas jets are activated, clouds of gas would remain in the room for the rest of the cutscene, instead of disappearing immediately as in the ''Old School'' version.
** Players would start being attacked by magic projectiles after the gas was activated, visibly lowering their health. The models and animations for the magic projectiles still exist in the game cache.
* Hazelmere did not originally start speaking to the player at the end of the quest, continuing to speak in their mind.

Various changes were made to [[Warped Tortoise]]s and [[Warped Terrorbird]]s:
* Warped creatures had their stats and drop tables rebalanced, alongside dropping the Old School-exclusive [[warped sceptre]].
* Warped terrorbirds originally had different defensive stats based on their appearance.
* Warped terrorbirds and warped tortoises were separate Slayer tasks that were automatically unlocked upon completion. In Old School RuneScape, both creatures share a single warped creature task, similar to [[spiritual creature]]s, and must be unlocked via the [[Slayer_Rewards#Unlock|Slayer Rewards]] shop. They also have their own [[Superior slayer monster|superior]] variants.
* The crystal chime originally had to be used on the warped creatures to begin fighting them, rather than just attacking them with the item present. Additionally, they would change their appearance and examine text after the chime was used on them. Standard warped terrorbirds now use the appearance they had after having the crystal chime used on them, while the boss versions fought at the end of the quest look like the pre-chime version.
* The crystal chime was originally made from the same [[crystal saw seed]], which meant players could not have both it and the [[crystal saw]], requiring a visit to the [[singing bowl]] in [[Brimstail's cave]] to switch. In ''Old School'', the chime is made from a separate item.
* Some of the warped creatures are in different locations. For example, there was not originally a warped tortoise right at the entrance, instead it was found upstairs next to the other tortoise.

The rewards have been slightly updated:
* The original only awarded one [[quest point]]; two are awarded in ''Old School''.
* Rather than rewarding experience directly after completion of the quest, players are rewarded with four [[Magic lamp (The Path of Glouphrie)|magic lamps]] instead, allowing players to claim the experience at their discretion.
*Originally, travelling via [[spirit tree]]s required the player to first travel to either the [[Gnome Stronghold]] or [[Tree Gnome Village (location)|Tree Gnome Village]] spirit trees before they could choose the destination they wanted to go. Completing the quest rewarded the ability to choose a destination from any spirit tree, but ''Old School'' had already implemented this in [[Update:Spirit trees, clues & more!|an update]] on [[1 May]] [[2014]]. Additionally, a new animation would play when using spirit trees after unlocking this ability during the quest. This is not present in ''Old School RuneScape'', but can be found within the game cache.

Other miscellaneous changes:
* The position of monoliths in the storeroom is now saved between visits, instead of resetting every time like in the original version. 
* The room with Yewnock's machine is now instanced like the rest of the storeroom.
* Watching the cutscenes in [[Bolrie]]'s diary is now required, rather than optional.
*Two [[unlisted music tracks]] were present in the original version, but not the Old School RuneScape version.
** A [[rsw:File:Mind Melding.ogg|creepy unlisted music track]] played when mind melding with Incomitatus.
** An [[rsw:File:The Terrorbirds.ogg|unlisted music track]] originally played when observing the terrorbirds at the end of the quest, before changing back to [[Terrorbird Tussle]] after being spotted.
* Walking close to the sewer exit would originally automatically take you outside the dungeon, instead of needing to select "Exit".
* The [[Poison Waste Dungeon]] did not originally contain any gas jets outside of the ones that appear in the cutscene at the end of the quest. As a result, their ability to damage players is exclusive to ''Old School''.

'''''Old School RuneScape'''''
*'''Developer(s):''' Mod Ed

==Trivia==
* The Path of Glouphrie was [[Backporting|ported from the original game]] with significant changes, as it was already nearly complete in the [[August 2007 Archive of RuneScape]]. It is the second quest to receive this treatment, after [[Land of the Goblins]].
**A bug present in the archived version also had to be fixed before The Path of Glouphrie could be released, which enabled players to claim the experience reward for this quest an indefinite number of times.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1702359492908687660|date=16 September 2023|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20230916204052/https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1702359492908687660|archivedate=16 September 2023|quote=(...) So this was a matter of merging it in, finishing the unfinished bits, fixing the infinite rewards bug from 2007 and redesigning the Slayer bit.}} By returning to a certain area in the Poison Waste Dungeon, the variable keeping track of the player's quest progression would revert to an earlier state, allowing one to trigger the final cutscene once more, and receive the associated rewards at the end.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1703036616774762547|date=16 September 2023|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20230916204312/https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1703036616774762547{{^|https://web.archive.org/web/20230916204457/https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1703116775213122016}}|archivedate=16 September 2023|quote=All the quest rewards - XP mostly. Something to do with walking back into a certain area after completing it, and getting the finale cutscene and quest rewards again. (...) I think it was fixed quickly. There's telemetry that flags quest progression going backwards like that, so quite likely there were only one or two people who encountered it - and social media wasn't such a big thing for RS back then.}}
* The addition of ''The Path of Glouphrie'' to ''Old School RuneScape'' was first hinted at in the [https://secure.runescape.com/m=news/gielinor-gazette---february-2022?oldschool=1 February 2022 Gielinor Gazette].
* The campaign posters in the cutscene from Bolrie's diary are written in [[Ancient Gnomish]], translated as "[Bolrie/Argenthorg] for king!"
* Bolrie's campaign poster appears to reference the ''{{Wp|Lord Kitchener Wants You}}'' recruitment poster for the British Army.
* If you examine Yewnock, it will say, "Can he copy it? Yes he can!" This is a reference to Oaknock's examine text, which is a reference to the children's TV show, ''{{wp|Bob the Builder}}''.
* Longramble mentions searching for the edge of the world in a conversation; this is a reference to the old myth of the world being flat.
* Gianne Jr. mentions that he couldn't find the coordinates of the delivery to Longramble the explorer on Doogle Maps (since his maps are written on dried [[doogle leaves]]). This is a reference to ''{{wp|Google Maps}}''.
* When speaking with Longramble for the first time, your character says: "Mr Longramble, I presume?" This mirrors a famous quote supposedly said by explorer {{Wp|Henry Morton Stanley}} when he found the missionary {{Wp|David Livingstone#Henry Morton Stanley|Dr David Livingstone}} in modern Tanzania after he had lost contact with the outside world.

'''The Ribbiting Tale of a Lily Pad Labour Dispute''', known by its shortened title '''Ribbiting Tale''', is a quest in [[Varlamore]] set in the [[Locus Oasis]] in which players solve a ribbiting dispute and gain access to a new [[Special_patches#Special_tree_patches|hardwood Farming patch]].

==Details==
{{Quest details
|start = Talk to [[Marcellus]] at the [[Locus Oasis]].
|startmap = 1684,2973
|difficulty = Novice
|description = Solve a ribbiting dispute and gain access to a new [[Special_patches#Special_tree_patches|hardwood Farming patch]].
|length = Very Short

** [[Children of the Sun]]
|items = * Any axe (a [[bronze axe]] is obtainable during the quest)
|recommended =

|leagueRegion = <poem>
{{LeagueRegion|Varlamore}} — location requirement
</poem>

==Walkthrough==
===Crazy Frogs===
[[File:Marcellus chathead.png|left]]
Speak to [[Marcellus]] at the [[Locus Oasis]] (fairy ring {{Fairycode|AJP}} - this is only accessible if you have visited Varlamore first), by the [[hardwood tree patch]]. He will appear to be crazy, accusing you of being in cahoots with the frogs at the other side of the oasis, believing that the frogs will enslave all of humanity.

Head to the centre of the oasis, just north of the grove of [[teak tree]]s, and speak to the blue frogs. They will tell you that they simply have gone on strike, as they believe Marcellus is mistreating them. You will then attempt to mediate between the two parties.

Return to Marcellus, who tells you that he refuses to make peace until they return his brain back, and will only negotiate with their leader.

===Democracy at Work===
{{Needed|An [[axe]]}}
Speak to [[Gary]] or [[Sue]], who will decide to hold an election to determine who leads, and reluctantly asks you to sabotage [[Cuthbert]]'s lily pad so that he does not win the vote in the frog-hopping competition, as they believe he will declare all out war with the humans. They will also ask that you do not let [[Dave]] and [[Jane]] spot you, as they are sticklers for the rules.

Speak to Dave or Jane, who you find has already set up the lily pads for the election. You will attempt to convince them to let you inspect the lily pads, but they refuse, believing it is their duty to look after them. They will note that they are hungry, and that the oranges nearby are considered a nice treat.

Chop down the [[Orange tree (Locus Oasis)|orange tree]] near them; if you did not bring an axe, the stump near Marcellus will give a [[bronze axe]]. With the both of them distracted, sabotage the lily pad.

Return to Gary and Sue, who will begin the election. A cutscene will play in which Sue and Cuthbert compete; Sue successfully hops on the lily pad, but Cuthbert sinks into the water and dies, as he never learned how to swim.

<gallery captionalign="center" widths="200">
The Ribbiting Tale of a Lily Pad Labour Dispute - chopping orange tree.png|Distracting Dave and Jane by cutting down an orange tree.
The Ribbiting Tale of a Lily Pad Labour Dispute - election hop-off.png|The frogs' Election Hop-Off begins.
</gallery>

===Peace Talks===
Now that Sue is the leader, she will negotiate with you and ask that in exchange for helping Marcellus by eating flies, he must pay the frogs with oranges. Take this offer to Marcellus, who will ask what the flies have done wrong. You will tell him that they are planning to kill him, but he wants proof of the flies' betrayal.
[[File:Chest (The Ribbiting Tale of a Lily Pad Labour Dispute) passcode.png|thumb|right|The interface displaying a passcode required to open the chest.]]
Return to Gary and Sue, who will suggest you steal something from Marcellus and pin it on the flies. Inside Marcellus' home, search his [[Bed (The Ribbiting Tale of a Lily Pad Labour Dispute)|bed]] for a [[love letter]]; reading it reveals he is in love with someone named Nalia, which is the passcode to the [[Chest (The Ribbiting Tale of a Lily Pad Labour Dispute)|chest]] in his home.

[[File:The Ribbiting Tale of a Lily Pad Labour Dispute - battling Cuthbert, Lord of Dread.png|thumb|300px|Cuthbert, Lord of Dread, returns with a vengeance.]]
Open the chest to retrieve a [[plushy]], then place it by the [[Capybara Dung|capybara dung]] to the east to plant the "evidence". However, upon doing so, [[Cuthbert, Lord of Dread]], is revealed to have survived the election and proceeds to attack the player. Cuthbert is a level-1 enemy and poses no meaningful threat. However, Cuthbert can still damage the player so can be killed with recoil damage for non-combat accounts. 

After your epic battle with Cuthbert, Lord of Dread, speak to Marcellus, who will now accept the frogs' terms. Finish up by talking to Sue or Gary to finish the quest.

'''Congratulations, quest complete!'''

==Trivia==
* The quest has the longest name of any in ''Old School RuneScape'', at 47 characters.
** The quest name contains the maximum amount of characters that the [[quest list]] currently allows.{{CiteVideo|author=XP Waste|title=HE DESIGNED THE PERILOUS MOONS Feat. Mod Rice|url=lcF_K8thXn4?t=11029|timestamp=03:03:50|date=28 March 2024|site=YouTube}}

* The update containing this quest was released on World Frog Day 2024, although it's unclear whether this was intentional.
* The quest contains multiple references to the {{WP|labour movement}}, such as the title and the variations of the phrase "a fair day's wage for a fair day's work" used throughout the quest. Other labour references include the frogs striking, [[Gary]]'s comments on capitalism, and the focus on collective leadership.
* During the [[2024 Summer Summit]], it was announced by [[Mod Ed]] that there would be a sequel. This was once again confirmed by Mod Ed at RuneFest 2025. *This is disputed by Mod Ed.

'''Twilight's Promise''' is the second quest in the [[Quests/Series#Twilight Emissaries|Twilight Emissaries]] series. It is set in the [[Civitas illa Fortis]] in eastern [[Varlamore]], and designed to introduce players to the kingdom and its features.

==Details==
{{Quest details
|start = Talk to [[Ennius Tullus]] or [[Furia Tullus]] in front of the [[Sunrise Palace]].
|startmap = 1686,3141
|difficulty = Intermediate
|description = Take your first steps into [[Varlamore]] and unlock the [[Quetzal Transport System]].
|length = Short
|requirements = * Completion of the following quests:
** [[Children of the Sun]]
|items = * Items for two different [[combat classes]] or a [[poisoned]] weapon (be warned that the poison method is much slower).
|recommended = * {{SCP|Combat|40|link=yes}}
* Some [[stamina potion]]s
* Food
|kills = * [[Knight of Varlamore (Twilight's Promise)|Knight of Varlamore]] (level 81)
* 8 [[cultist]]s (level 34)
|leagueRegion = <poem>
Unlocking {{LeagueRegion|Varlamore}} {{okay}} will auto-complete the quest
</poem>
}}

==Walkthrough==
===With friends like these...===
[[File:Ennius Tullus chathead.png|left]]
Talk to [[Regulus Cento]] outside [[Varrock|Varrock's]] east gate to travel to [[Varlamore]]. When you arrive, speak to [[Ennius Tullus|Ennius]] or [[Furia Tullus]] at the entrance to the [[Sunrise Palace]] in [[Civitas illa Fortis]]. You will be instructed to visit the temple in the city, as [[Prince Itzla]] is expecting you. The temple is found just south-east of the [[bazaar]], marked on the world map with two [[File:Dungeon map link icon.png]] dungeon icons.

At the temple, you will find [[Metzli, Teokan of Ranul]], who will tell you that you saved the life of her counterpart, [[Servius]]. Tell her you're meant to be meeting the prince, and Metzli will tell you he is talking to Servius in the crypt under the temple. Take the stairs down to proceed.

After entering the crypt, head north through the gate and speak to the prince in the centre of the open area. He will re-introduce you to [[Servius, Teokan of Ralos]], revealing him to be his father, and will remind you that someone is plotting to kill Servius. He will then explain that, given the strict policies on travelling outside the kingdom before the signing of the treaty in Varrock, the culprit can only be a member of the delegation that visited. Prince Itzla therefore suspects that one of the [[Knight of Varlamore (Children of the Sun)|Knights of Varlamore]] who travelled with Servius is responsible, and suggests speaking with the Tullus twins once more.

===Oh Brother!===
[[File:Varlamore crest detail.png|left|73px]]
Return to the Tullus twins at the [[Sunrise Palace]], who are now found further inside the palace grounds. They will mention six knights and give you their locations, as well as a [[Varlamore crest]] to prove you are helping them. You must now find and collect the [[Knight of Varlamore (Children of the Sun)|knights]], who will all be known as "Knight(s) of Varlamore". They do not have to be returned to the palace in any particular order. 

====Arrun and Claudia====
[[File:Twilight's Promise - pickpocking stolen amulet.png|thumb|220px|The correct citizen to steal the stolen amulet from.]]
Arrun and Claudia can be found in the centre of the [[bazaar]]. They will agree to return to the palace after finishing their work of catching a thief, for whom they planted an amulet at one of the stalls, hoping it would be stolen. They will encourage you to rummage through the pockets of bazaar-goers until you find the thief that took the bait.

Pickpocket the male [[Citizen (Twilight's Promise)|citizen]] in the second-to-lightest shade of blue robes (he will be the only one with robes of that colour, see picture) to find the [[stolen amulet]]. Return it to the knights, and at which point they will agree to return to the palace.

====Nel====
[[File:Twilight's Promise - weapons crate.png|thumb|220px|The crate full of weapons.]]
Nel can be found in the south-western part of the [[Fortis Cothon]], on the docks. To help her return to the palace quicker, she will ask for assistance in finding a [[Crate (Twilight's Promise)|crate]] full of weapons. Complete the dialogue until Nel mentions where to find the crate, and then head to the north-east corner of the cothon.

The crate you will need to search is directly adjacent to two barrels with fish in them, close to a bench. Search the crate to learn the name of the smuggling ship, the Fortis Spark, and return to Nel. Inform her of your findings and she will agree to return to the palace.

====Mezan====
{{Needed|Combat equipment for two different styles, or a poisoned weapon (there is a bank in the Colosseum that requires [[Glory]] to use).}}
Upon entering the [[Fortis Colosseum|Colosseum]], head north to the training area and talk to Mezan. He will mention that his training partner has not shown up, and will only leave if you spar with him in the partner's place. The fight will require any two combat styles, as he will start praying against the one currently being used every four attacks. If no attack style is used 4 times in a row (for instance, attack 3 times with melee then once with range and repeat) then he will never use protection prayers. It is also possible to use a [[poisoned]] weapon to finish Mezan off, as this can be reapplied through his prayers. Once the fight is over, Mezan will leave for the palace. If the player dies at the same time as the knight then the knight will still return to the castle when spoken to.

Note: The Voidwaker special attack counts as a non-melee based attack.

Note: [[skillers]] and other limited account builds can use [[poison dynamite]] to poison Mezan and run in circles until he dies. Players can also use dynamite for true damage dealt on him, and then recoil him down to 0. Mezan's max hit is 8, meaning that players doing this method should be prepared with a substantial amount of food as well as [[Saradomin brews]].

====Velam and Azali====
[[File:Twilight's Promise - Velam sobering up.png|thumb|250px|The player instructs Azali to dunk her head in the fountain in order to sober up.]]
Velam and Azali can be found at [[Atlazora's Rest]], just north of the [[Outer Fortis General Store]]. Azali will need to sober up, so lead her to the fountain east of the bar to trigger a short [[cutscene]]. Once in a while, Azali will stop following you; simply talk to her again and then head towards the fountain once more. Return to the bar and speak to Velam, and then head to the palace after finishing the conversation. If you have a pet or follower active, Azali will not follow you.

====Judgement====
[[File:Twilight's Promise - Velam is killed.png|thumb|250px|Ennius kills Velam, who pleaded his innocence until the very end.]]
Once all knights have returned to the palace, speak to the twins again to learn that the knights stayed in the [[Kualti Headquarters]] prior to visiting Varrock, just west of the palace. The Headquarters is the large building containing a statue of [[Queen Zyanyi Arkan]], situated across the road from a small building with training dummies. Head north-west and go up both flights of stairs to reach their bedrooms.

Investigate one of the [[Chest (Twilight's Promise)|chest]]s in the south-eastern room to find an [[incriminating letter]] (the letter has an equal chance of being in either chest), and then read it and return to the twins once more. Speaking to the twins will trigger a cutscene in which Velam, claiming innocence, will be killed by Ennius. The twins will now tell you to deliver the news to the prince at [[the Teomat]]. '''Note:''' reading the letter is '''required''' to start the cutscene.

===The Twilight Emissaries===
Speak to [[Regulus Cento]] south-east of the palace next to the quetzals and ask about getting to the Teomat. Regulus will tell you that Prince Itzla has given you a personal [[quetzal]] to fly around Varlamore, and gives you some [[Quetzal feed (Twilight's Promise)|quetzal feed]] for [[Renu]], who is newly trained and ready. Feed Renu the quetzal feed, and an interface for the [[Quetzal Transport System]] will open. Travel to [[the Teomat]] (it will be a small option on the menu that looks like a tiny house on top of mountains, found just north of the [[Cam Torum]] location). From here on, the quetzal system is unlocked.

Head inside the Teomat and speak to Prince Itzla in the room with the altar icon, and let him know about Velam's betrayal. He will be surprised, and when you tell him that you believe that Velam's murder is too convenient and that Ennius had killed him too quickly, he will agree to keep an eye on the twins. He will then share to you about the [[Twilight Emissaries]], a religious cult obsessed with the end of the world - the Final Dawn.

To learn about the Final Dawn, head slightly north to the library and speak with [[Metzli]]. She will mention [[Ximoua]], a belief passed down from the [[Old Ones]], and say that the Final Dawn being an interpretation of it; the difference in belief however is not that the end of the world ''will'' come, but rather that it must be ''made''. As you're finishing up the conversation, you will be attacked by eight level 34 [[cultist]]s, whom the guards must defeat. Note that only one will attack you; the rest will only attack after being attacked first. If necessary, you may let the guards kill the cultists.

Once you defeat all eight cultists, a cutscene will play showing that Servius has been gravely wounded, even though none of the cultists made it inside. Notably, [[Metzli]] has disappeared, but Servius is quickly brought back to the capital. Prince Itzla will then tell you that he will contact you again once he has planned the next steps.

==Walkthrough==
===Infiltration===
[[File:The Heart of Darkness - the Sun Queen arrives.png|thumb|250px|Queen Zyanyi Arkan arrives at the Teomat to speak to her son.]]
Start the quest where you left off at the end of [[Twilight's Promise]], at [[the Teomat]]. Speak to [[Prince Itzla]], who will propose you and him go undercover by infiltrating the [[Twilight Emissaries]]. As he discusses the plan, his mother, [[Queen Zyanyi Arkan]], will arrive. Frustrated at her son's failure to protect his father, Itzla tells her about his plans to lead the infiltration. However, she refuses, insisting that he confide in someone he absolutely trusts to lead in his stead. After the Queen's departure, Itzla relents and asks you to visit a pub in the [[Quetzacalli Gorge]] to meet a trusted contact of his, who will fill you in on the infiltration operation.

Head south-west towards [[Renu]] and fly to the Quetzacalli Gorge, then head to [[the Windbreaker]] pub and speak to the bartender. Ask him to rent the basement room as instructed, only to find out a basement doesn't exist; he will offer to let you rent the ground floor room for 30 coins instead. If you don't have 30 coins, either pickpocket the citizens around the area or use the bank just east of the pub. Once you have the coins, accept the bartender's offer, then head to the east room and rest at the [[Bed (The Heart of Darkness)|bed]].

Upon waking up, you will find a disguised Prince Itzla to be your "trusted contact". He claims that there are very few people he can trust after the events of the previous quest, and that the less people who know about his mission, the better; additionally, as an outsider fairly uninvolved in Varlamorian politics, you ironically are far more trustworthy. He will then tell you that he believes a shopkeeper in the Gorge is recruiting members for the cult, and that you will pose as a potential recruit in the hopes he'll contact the Emissaries.

Head out east to the [[Quetzacalli Gorge General Store]] and speak to the shopkeeper, and tell him that you've heard he can offer help to those in need. He is initially skeptical, but accepts your request to join the Emissaries, and tells you and your "friend" to head to the Twilight Temple, where he'll send word for them to expect two recruits. Return to Prince Itzla at [[the Windbreaker]], he will then meet you at the Temple.

===Trials of the Emissaries===
{{Needed|4 empty inventory slots|recommended=10 [[Quetzal feed]], 3 [[limestone brick]]s, and 4 [[soft clay]]. Combat gear, Food, [[Prayer Potion]]s and at least 43+ prayer for [[Protect from Melee]]}}
Head north-east past the gate, and make your way east past [[the Proudspire]], then head south to the [[Tower of Ascension]] to meet Prince Itzla. He will tell you that a person named [[Forebearer Janus]] will call on the both of you when its time to be tested. In the meantime, he wishes to speak to the nearby recruits for insights on why they wish to join the Emissaries.

Talk to the nearby recruits: [[Nova]], [[Sergius]], [[Felius]], and [[Caritta]]. Nova will speak of the Augur, the new leader of the Emissaries, who has reorganized the cult and is said to guide them to Mokhaiotl. Return to Prince Itzla, who will explain that Mokhaiotl refers to the centre of the world, which is where it is said [[Ximoua]] will happen. As you discuss this with him, [[Forebearer Janus]] calls on the both of you to begin your trials.

Before leaving, it is recommended that you bring the materials to build a [[landing site]]: 10 [[quetzal feed]], 3 [[limestone brick]]s, and 4 [[soft clay]], as you'll be in proximity to the [[Salvager Overlook]] landing site en route to the Temple.

====The first trial====
[[File:The Heart of Darkness - Emissaries' first trial.png|thumb|250px|The first trial of the Twilight Emissaries.]]
{{Cquote2|The aim is simple: Speak the correct pass phrase to me and you will be allowed to proceed.}}

You will be in a room with three [[Emissary Ascended]]. Pickpocket one of them to obtain a [[Tower key (The Heart of Darkness)|tower key]], which is used to open the south-east gate. Search the chest to receive a [[Book (The Heart of Darkness)|book]] and [[scrap of paper]]. Take note of the first letter of each white word in the book, which is the passcode for the south-western chest; you will receive a [[poem]] and another scrap of paper.

The first word of each verse in the poem uses the language of the [[Old Ones]], translated as cardinal directions: Takam = East, Makt = North, Silam = West, Uitt = South. Reference the poem to get the order of arrows for the code for the last chest located in the north-west part of the room. Enter the code to get the last scrap of paper. Combine the three for a [[completed note]], which contains a pass phrase.

Speak the pass phrase to Forebearer Janus to complete the first trial.

====The second trial====
[[File:The Heart of Darkness - Emissaries' second trial.png|thumb|250px|The second trial of the Twilight Emissaries.]]
{{Cquote2|Welcome to your next trial. Here, there is one simple goal... Survive.}}

The second trial is combat-based, with [[Emissary Brawler]]s (melee) and [[Emissary Conjurer]]s (magic) attacking two at a time, then four at a time. The level 86 brawlers can use a special attack that strikes the tiles adjacent to them, while the conjurers can heal themselves and adjacent brawlers. These special attacks are marked by black shadows appearing on the ground. Players should take care to move out of the brawlers' special attack as it can hit through prayer. The prince is able to dodge this attack on his own.

There are a total of four waves:
* Wave 1: Two level 74 brawlers initially, with two reinforcements replacing them as each falls.
* Wave 2: One level 74 and one level 86 brawler initially, with two reinforcements of the same kind.
* Wave 3: One level 86 brawler and one conjurer initially, which are replaced by one level 74 brawler and another conjurer.
* Wave 4: Two level 86 brawlers and two conjurers at the same time, with no reinforcements.

Both you and Prince Itzla must survive the trial; use the [[Bandages (The Heart of Darkness)|bandages]] from the [[medical box]]es around the room on him to heal. There are a total of three boxes with five bandages each, and will heal 18 hitpoints to Prince Itzla. The bandages can also be used on yourself, but will heal less{{Clarify|12 HP from one source, unsure if this scales}} than when used on the prince. Lower level players who cannot clear the trial quickly should be careful to leave enough to heal him. 

If Prince Itzla dies, you will fail the trial and have to restart. The bandage boxes will be refilled.

Speak to Forebearer Janus again to start the third trial. Any remaining bandages should be used to heal before this as they will be removed upon proceeding.

====The third trial====
[[File:The Heart of Darkness - Emissaries' third trial.png|thumb|250px|The third trial of the Twilight Emissaries.]]
{{Cquote2|Welcome to your third trial. Before you stand some recently initiated acolytes. However, it seems one of them was not as loyal to our cause as first believed. Your task is to question all four and determine who the traitor is.}}

The third trial involves questioning the members of the cult - [[Tenoch]], [[Silia]], [[Adrius]], and [[Eleuia]] - and working out who the traitor is. Ask each of them either why they joined the Emissaries or what they know about the Final Dawn; '''the traitor (different for each player) will always mention [[Ranul|''Mictl'']]'''. Mictl (the afterlife in the [[Losanium]] religion) not only doesn't exist in the religion of the Twilight Emissaries, but is also in conflict with its cyclic cosmological model, where the world is periodically destroyed and rebuilt into a new one. Once you question each member, you'll be given the option to accuse them while talking to them. If none of the members mention Mictl, you may need to exit and re-enter the floor. 

If the chosen member is the traitor, Janus will kill them rather than keep them barely alive; speak to him to begin the final trial.

====The fourth trial====
[[File:The Heart of Darkness - Emissaries' fourth trial.png|thumb|250px|The final trial of the Twilight Emissaries.]]
{{Cquote2|Victory is within your reach, but one more trial awaits... Face your opponent.}}

The final trial requires you to battle Prince Itzla. He uses melee attacks, so [[Protect from Melee]] is advised. He will use protection prayers whenever you perform a [[special attack]], and uses two in turn, both of which he will warn you about in advance. For instance, he will pray [[Protect from Magic]] if a Voidwaker special is used.

The sword swipe special attack turns off any active protection prayers, but you can simply reactivate them without any delay. The other is an AoE attack, once he warns you he is going to do it, run behind him immediately to dodge.

Upon his defeat, speak to Janus to complete the trials.

===The Ruins of Tapoyauik===
{{Needed|up to 4 empty inventory slots (the icons can be done one at a time, but is recommended against)|recommended=Combat gear, Food, [[Prayer Potion]]s}}
[[File:The Heart of Darkness - Metzli appears.png|thumb|250px|The Augur is revealed to be Metzli, the Teokan of Ranul.]]
Now that you and Prince Itzla have passed the trials, the Augur herself will oversee the initiation process. Open the nearby chest to obtain the [[Twilight Emissary Robes]], then wear them and make your way to the [[Twilight Temple]] to begin a cutscene. 

'''''Note:''' If you teleport out or walk too far, Itzla will go back to the Tower of Ascension.''

During the initation, it is revealed that the Augur is indeed [[Augur Metzli|Metzli]], the Teokan of Ranul, and claims [[Ennius Tullus|Ennius]] and [[Furia Tullus]] are the mortal forms of [[Ralos]] and [[Ranul]], who were reborn as the twins during an eclipse 31 years ago.

After the cutscene, speak to [[Forebearer Fides]]. She will task you with opening up the passage to the [[Ruins of Tapoyauik]], a fortress of the [[Old Ones]] under the temple, where Metzli believes they left behind secrets to bring about the Final Dawn. Make your way to the building directly south, and climb down the stairs to the blocked passage; a [[barrel (Ruins of Tapoyauik)|barrel]] containing pickaxes can be found nearby to mine it.
[[File:The Heart of Darkness - past blockage.png|thumb|250px|Frost nagua manifest before the cultists.]]
Upon mining the blockage, a cutscene will play in which you proceed further into the fortress. However, the ground rumbles, manifesting two [[frost nagua]], killing [[Forebearer Vulcan]] and knocking Prince Itzla over a pit.

'''Note:''' Once you have completed the cutscene, you no longer need to wear the [[Twilight Emissary Robes]] to proceed. The robes will be required in the subsequent quest [[The Final Dawn]], and can be reclaimed at anytime from the chest you found them in.

You will now need to navigate the fortress to meet up with Prince Itzla. Run past the frost nagua (use [[Protect from Magic]] if able), then avoid the spear traps; getting hit by one will stun you and deal 6-12 damage. Once past them, '''pull the [[Lever (Ruins of Tapoyauik)|lever]]''' and climb down the nearby ledge.
[[File:The Heart of Darkness - navigating Tapoyauik.png|thumb|250px|Navigating the Ruins of Tapoyauik.]]
Next, run past the [[frost crab]]s and make your way north, avoiding stepping on the [[Trap (Ruins of Tapoyauik)|traps]] by taking the middle path. You will come across a wall by an icy ledge that you can slide across. Once across, enter the north-eastern room and move around the trap before '''pulling the lever'''. Move west to the [[frozen platform]]s and cross them, then climb down the western ledge.

Head west to the enclosed room and '''pull another lever''', avoiding the trap. Head south to find a large gate and another '''lever to pull''' on the north side. Before entering, pull the chain just east to unlock a shortcut to the exit. If you need to leave and come back, climb down the stairs to enter the dungeon and head west to climb down this chain.

There are four total levers to pull, each lever lighting a brazier at the large gate.

====Icons Puzzle====

When you walk west through the gate, you will find yourself in a large, rectangular room divided into thirds. The eastern third that you start in contains many urns and two murals. The middle third has a floor of ice and several frost nagua. The western third contains urns, another two murals, four statues, and a frozen door.

'''Do not search the urns yet''' - whilst searching urns, frost naguas will spawn and attack and cannot be safespotted. Instead, inspect the two murals and take note of the first words used (zema, oma, yeya, naui) and the corresponding element that is visible on them. You will need to recall these word-element pairs soon. Then, run all the way west to meet up with Prince Itzla. He will help you fight any nagua that you bring near him.

Now in the western third of the room, inspect the other two murals for their words and elements. Check which three of the statues are broken. Then, you will need to run back east again.

In the eastern third again, search the urns to find three distinct [[Icon (The Heart of Darkness)|icons]] which correspond to the broken statues that you inspected earlier. The icons will be found in the urns corresponding to their elements, but there are multiple possible urns for each icon. Incorrect urns will spawn a frost nagua that will attack and chase you around the room. Once you have all three icons, run west again.

Finally, in the western third again, use the icons on their corresponding statues. Once you have done so, you will need to touch each of the four statues in the correct order. The words on the murals determine the order in which the player must touch the statues: Zema = 1, Oma = 2, Yeya = 3, and Naui = 4. Meanwhile, the elements on the murals determine the specific statue that must be touched. The order is different for each player. If all statues are touched, but in the incorrect order, you will take damage from falling rocks.

Upon touching the statues correctly, they will unleash a wave spell, melting the ice off the door and killing any remaining frost naguas near it. The next section will be a boss fight, so return to a bank if needed.
[[File:The Ruins of Tapoyauik Levers 1.png|thumb|width=225x225|The location of the first lever, pulled after traversing the first wall traps.]]

===Guardian of the Fortress===
{{Instance}}
{{Needed|Combat gear (Melee combat strongly recommended)|recommended=Food, [[Prayer Potion]]s and at least 37 prayer to use [[Protect from Magic]], [[Super combat potion]]s or similar, melee equipment to destroy ice blocks (Glacial temotli)}}
[[File:The Ruins of Tapoyauik Levers 2.png|thumb|width=225x225|The location of the second lever, within the north-eastern room between the sliding wall and the platform jumps.]]
Enter the door to begin a cutscene in which you and Prince Itzla encounter [[Amoxliatl]], a powerful frost nagua guarding the fortress. She will tell you and Itzla that the Mokhaiotl - or the Tlati archive - is off-limits to humans, claiming they are unworthy. Suddenly, Prince Itzla is teleported away, revealing that [[Metzli]], [[Ennius Tullus|Ennius]], and [[Furia Tullus|Furia]] followed you here. As they attempt to deal with you, Amoxliatl claims they have defiled Tapoyauik and will face the consequences. However, as they teleport away, you are forced to fight her in their stead.

<gallery captionalign="center" widths="200">
The Heart of Darkness - Amoxliatl.png|The player and Prince Itzla encounter Amoxliatl.
The Heart of Darkness - Metzli and the Tullus twins.png|Metzli and the Tullus twins reveal themselves.
</gallery>

The quest version of Amoxliatl is somewhat easier than the regular fight, possessing 400 hitpoints instead of 520 and having more forgiving damage. Nevertheless, players will still have to properly handle her mechanics to beat the fight.

Amoxliatl uses three different attacks. In her standard attack, she attacks with magic, summoning ice spikes on the player's current tile and around the arena. [[Protect from Magic]] will protect against the initial attack, but the ice spikes additionally deal typeless damage. Finally, an icy pool will be left on the tile where the player was originally standing that will deal 6-10 damage per tick.
[[File:The Ruins of Tapoyauik Levers 3.png|thumb|width=228x228|The location of the third and fourth levers. The third lever is in the last north-western room. The fourth lever is directly north of the ancient gate, in close proximity to the braziers.]]
[[File:Fighting Amoxliatl.png|thumb|250px|The player fights Amoxliatl, the guardian of Tapoyauik.]]
After every 2-4 standard attacks, Amoxliatl will use one of two special attacks. The first one used is randomly selected, but after that, she will alternate between them and will not use the same special attack twice in a row. If you are standing in the narrow entry path, she will not use her Unstable Ice special attack.

* Unstable ice blocks: Amoxliatl forms 1-4 blocks of unstable ice around the arena. If not destroyed in time (16 ticks, ~10 seconds), all remaining ice blocks will shatter, causing icy pools to form within 3x3 of the ice blocks and healing the boss (16-25) for each ice block shattered. The ice blocks can only be destroyed with melee, and melee attacks against them will result in a max hit with an attack speed of 1. 

* Icicle attack: Amoxliatl disables the player's prayer and launches an icicle at them. A message is shown in the chatbox: {{mes|Amoxliatl disables your prayers and launches an icicle attack!|colour=red}} Turn on [[Protect from Magic]] before the icicle hits you to negate all damage.

After defeating Amoxliatl, you will forcefully be banished from Tapoyauik. Make your way to [[Sunrise Palace]], where [[Servius]] is currently staying. You will inform him of the events that transpired, and he will ask that you leave so as to avoid the Queen's anger, but assures you that you will be involved in whatever plans are made next.

It involves meeting [[Floopa]], an [[Injured Tortugan]], stranded on a [[Remote Island]] in the [[Unquiet Ocean]], who needs your help to get back to the [[Great Conch]]. Through her, the player learns more about Tortugan society and the threat posed by the [[gryphon]]s. Completion of the quest unlocks access to the Great Conch. ==Details== {{Quest details |start = Talk to the [[injured tortugan]] on a [[Remote Island]] in the [[Unquiet Ocean]]. |startmap = 2958,2606 |difficulty = Experienced |description = Help a stranded tortugan and gain access to the Great Conch. |length = Medium |requirements = * {{SCP|Slayer|51|link=yes}} {{Boostable|no}} {{Questreqstart|yes}} * {{SCP|Construction|48|link=yes}}{{Boostable|no}} {{Questreqstart|yes}} * {{SCP|Sailing|45|link=yes}}{{Boostable|no}} {{Questreqstart|yes}} * {{SCP|Hunter|45|link=yes}}{{Boostable|no}} {{Questreqstart|yes}} * {{SCP|Woodcutting|40|link=yes}}{{Boostable|no}} {{Questreqstart|yes}} * {{SCP|Crafting|34|link=yes}}{{Boostable|no}} {{Questreqstart|yes}} *Completion of [[Pandemonium]] |items = * Any [[axe]] (a bronze axe can be found during the quest, but bringing a better one is recommended for cutting 10 logs) * [[Hammer]] (obtainable during the quest) or [[Imcando hammer]] * [[Saw]] (obtainable during the quest) or [[Amy's saw]] |recommended = * At least 4 free inventory spaces (or up to 22 for all the construction materials at once, as there is a bank easily accessible) * {{SCP|Combat|60|link=yes}} * Food and combat gear * [[Stamina Potion]] |kills = *[[Gryphon]] (level 95) *[[Shellbane gryphon]] (level 235) |ironman = |leagueRegion = Not accessible in the [[Demonic Pacts League]] }} ==Walkthrough== === Finding Floopa === Using your [[boat]], head to the remote island north-west of [[The Great Conch]], marked on the map with the [[Quests|quest]] icon [[File:Quest start icon.png|frameless]]. Talk to the [[Injured Tortugan|injured tortugan]] to attempt to help her, and she will decline your assistance. Eventually, the tortugan will reluctantly accept your aid, and ask you to make some bandages with nearby resources. Shake the palm trees for a [[palm leaf]], then pick up a nearby [[seaweed]] spawn, and use the items on each other to create [[makeshift bandages]]. Give the bandages to the tortugan, who will then introduce herself as [[Floopa]]. Offer to take Floopa home and she'll again refuse your help, this time believing that returning home would mean failing everything. Eventually, she will begrudgingly agree, and let you bring her back home to [[the Great Conch]]. Floopa will then board your [[boat]] and will remain there even if the boat capsizes or is abandoned. === The Great Conch === [[File:Raley and Floopa.png|thumb|width=275x275|Floopa, back home at Elder Raley's.]] Sail south-east from where you found Floopa, making your way to the pier at the southern end of the Great Conch. Disembark and head up the docks to find Floopa, alongside [[Elder Korel]]. :'''Note''': [[Fairy ring]] {{Fairycode|CJQ}}'' '' will now be unlocked, allowing you to return to the island at any time. Speak to Floopa, and Elder Korel will send her to [[Elder Raley]]'s hut. Elder Korel will then ask you to leave, as the tortugans are not fond of humans; you'll insist on staying until she recovers, causing Elder Korel to allow you on the island as a "tourist." He will mention that in order to stay permanently, you will need to become a honorary tortugan. He will then direct you to Elder Raley's hut, found just east of the entrance to the town (marked on the map with a [[range]] icon [[File:Cooking range icon.png|frameless]]). === Making repairs === {{Needed|[[hammer]], [[saw]], [[axe]], 10 [[jatoba logs]], 6 [[sea shell]]s, 6 [[tortugan scute]]s}} Speak to Floopa inside Elder Raley's hut, and Elder Raley will tell her that the village was attacked by [[gryphons]]. While no one died, the village was damaged in the scuffle. They will then notice you, with Floopa surprised to see that you were still waiting for her. You explain to them that Korel allowed you to stay as a tourist, and offer to help fix the damage, causing Elder Raley to thank you and give you a [[list of repairs]]. You will now need to make six repairs in the town centre, marked by several [[shop]] icons. Each repair gives 80 [[Construction]] experience. {{map|mapID=0|zoom=3|align=right|caption=Repair locations

A [[hammer]] and [[saw]] also spawn in the village, in the blacksmith's workshop to the north-east and in [[Elder Raley]]'s house respectively. Once all repairs are done, return to Elder Raley. [[File:Gryphon cave.png|thumb|width=275x275|The cave where the [[Gryphon|gryphon]] is nesting. ]] === Tracking the attacker === {{Needed|Axe, combat gear}} As you return, Floopa will lament the permanent damage to her flipper. Raley will reassure her that the village will be there for her, at which point you will inform Raley that the repairs are done. Elder will now ask for your help finding and killing the gryphon that attacked the village, saying it's only a matter of time before it returns. Since the gryphon was injured in battle, it wasn't able to fly away; however, it retreated into the forest, and you'll now have to track it. Head to the statue in the centre of the village and inspect it to reveal some tracks. Follow these tracks west, then examine the spiky red plant found at the split in the path. Follow the tracks north, and inspect the rockslide, then continue north once more and inspect the plant immediately east of the passage entrance. You'll come to a cluster of three plants; inspect the eastern plant to find the final set of tracks, which takes you to a cave entrance. Use your axe to clear the growth blocking the cave, and enter it to begin a fight with a level 95 [[gryphon]]. The gryphon only attacks with [[melee]], but it will also use a special attack that knocks the player back and deals moderate damage if their '''worn weight''' is not high enough. To avoid taking any damage, simply stand next to the wall and pray [[Protect from Melee]]. Once the gryphon is dead, report back to Elder Raley. [[File:Battle at the Little Pearl.png|thumb|width=350x350|Tortugans fighting to protect their eggs.]] === Pearl in peril === {{Needed|combat gear, prayer, food, and a [[tortugan shield]]}} You'll return to Elder Raley's hut to find Elder Korel informing him of another gryphon attack, this time on the Little Pearl. Elder Korel will immediately depart, as this is where tortugans lay their eggs. Elder Raley will ask you to help Elder Korel, but since the gryphon appears to be one of the larger ones, he'll direct you to [[Elder Blunn]] for further preparation. Grab any gear, food and supplies from the bank before speaking to Elder Blunn, then speak to him in the marketplace to receive a [[tortugan shield]]. Head back to the dock and sail to the Little Pearl, which is south-east from the dock. When you arrive, you will see a cutscene in which a strange ship quickly departs, leaving elders Korel, [[Elder Hubber|Hubber]], and [[Elder Root|Root]] engaged in battle with a [[shellbane gryphon]]. ==== The fight ==== As soon as the cutscene ends, the gryphon will attack. Activate [[Protect from Melee]] if attacking from up close, otherwise go with [[Protect from Missiles]] and stand near the ocean shore where the gryphon can't reach you directly. The tortugan shield '''must be equipped''' for the entire fight, or else the gryphon's attacks will deal heavy damage that ignores protection prayers. The gryphon will use both melee and ranged auto-attacks and occasionally line up a special attack: {| class="wikitable" !Attack !Attack !Negation |- |Slam |The gryphon will knock the player back and deal heavy damage if '''[[Weight|worn weight]]''' is less than 40kg. |Wear [[Shellbane_gryphon/Strategies#Equipment|heavy equipment]], or any items with a [[gold helmet]]. Alternatively, stand out of reach: behind a tree or eggs or near the ocean shore. |- |Whirlwinds |The gryphon will flap its wings, creating whirlwinds on the player's location that can hit for 50+. |Moving around during the flapping sequence will prevent the whirlwind from growing and hurting you. |- |Corrosive spit |The gryphon will spit orange acid on the player's current tile, causing a [[corrosion]] effect. |Step at least one tile away from the spit before it lands. |} [[File:Troubled_Tortugans_-_Mysterious_ship_cutscene.mp4|thumb|300px|The mysterious ship seen fleeing the scene of the gryphon attack.]] If you die during the fight, your gravestone will appear where you last docked, and the ship you moored at the Little Pearl will be considered Lost, requiring recovery at a [[Shipwright]]. Dying to the Gryphon's whirlwind attack after reducing its HP to 0 will still progress the quest. Players having trouble fighting the Gryphon may hide behind the palm trees and let the Tortugans lower its health to 20 hitpoints. Speak to Elder Korel after killing the gryphon, and he will question how the gryphon went so far from the conch. You will then tell him about the strange ship with red sails leaving the island as you came, and he'll suggest you inform Elder Raley. Head back to Elder Raley's hut and tell him and Floopa about the ship, and Floopa recalls being betrayed by her crew and thrown overboard. She'll comment that might be a connection between the events, but will need time to think about it further. Raley will tell her to rest and allows you to explore the island in the meantime, promising to call you when Floopa has recovered. '''Congratulations, quest complete!''' ==Rewards== {{Quest rewards |name = Troubled Tortugans |image = [[File:Troubled Tortugans reward scroll.png|centre|488px]] |qp = 1 |rewards = *{{SCP|Sailing|10,000|link=yes}} experience *{{SCP|Slayer|8,000|link=yes}} experience *Access to the [[Great Conch]] and its facilities (such as the [[fairy ring]] {{fairycode|CJQ}} and [[notice board]]) *Ability to fight [[gryphon]]s }} ==Required for completing== Completion of Troubled Tortugans is required for the following: * [[The Red Reef]] ==Transcript== {{Hastranscript|quest}} ==Music== {| class="wikitable sortable" !Name ! class="unsortable" |Unlock details ! class="unsortable" |Music track |- |[[The Tortugan Way]] |Unlocked on [[The Great Conch]] |[[File:The Tortugan Way.ogg]] |- |[[Elder Wisdom]] |Unlocked on [[The Great Conch]] |[[File:Elder Wisdom.ogg]] |- |[[Below the Conch]] |Unlocked in the [[Gryphon Caves]] |[[File:Below the Conch.ogg]] |- |[[What the Shell!]] |Unlocked in the fight with the [[Shellbane gryphon|shellbane gryphon]] |[[File:What the Shell!.ogg]] |} {{Troubled Tortugans}} {{Sailing}}
